docs.landing.component: A THING PUT DOWN BESIDE ANOTHER THING DOES NOT SHOVE IT ASIDE.
Collision without that distinction has to pick one wrong answer and live with it: either a die
dropped from above buries the chip it lands on, or setting a die down next to a chip flicks the
chip across the felt. Neither is a desk anybody has played on.
So what is already lying there HOLDS ITS PLACE — still solid, so nothing comes to rest on top
of it, and moved by nothing that merely fell. Something genuinely travelling arrives and it is
an ordinary body again, and goes skidding. Only the desk can tell those apart, because only the
desk knows whether a hand threw or let go.
docs.landing.scene: LANDING — drop a handful of dice onto a block of chips and not one chip moves.
Take the dice by their handle, move nothing, and let go. They come down among the chips, find
room between them and settle. The block is still the block: every chip exactly where it was.
Now turn the throw on and send the same handful into the same block. Every chip it reaches goes
skidding. Same pieces, same room, same worlds — what changed is that the hand was going
The threshold is the desk's own: the same speed that decides whether a released piece flies at
all decides whether it shoves, so "thrown" means one thing here and not two. The neighbouring
page, Collision, is this desk with the throw on — the pair is the lesson.
